answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation stake before it can vote on a task, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits expose fabricated work. A sparrow account may be cheap to create, but a swarm of such accounts cannot multiply its influence without multiplying capital at risk; the attacker must fund every identity and keep each one honest enough to avoid forfeiture. A quill-signed audit record makes penalties attributable, not just a fable about trust.
